  A comment after the final semicolon is fine.
- PIVOT and UNPIVOT work only inside a subquery: `SELECT * FROM (PIVOT ...)`.

  tables below and table functions that generate data, such as `range`, only.
- A result may have at most 5,000 rows, and a query may run for at most 10 seconds. Past

  raw readings.

content.thinking: I need to check whether the department readings table has any data, since the meter might only have readings or I may have to sum the machines instead. I also want to confirm the month_start format. Next I'll run one exploratory query on readings by month, along with a sum over the machines, and then take the difference between March and February.

input.sql: SELECT meter_id, month_start, sum(kwh), count(*) FROM reading WHERE meter_id IN ('dept_d','line_d1','line_d2') AND local_date >= '2026-02-01' AND local_date < '2026-04-01' GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY 1,2

content.thinking: I'm checking the March interval count, which works out to 2972 after the DST adjustment, and February's 2688 looks right too. The totals match, so there's no sign of duplicates. The line items sum to 26194.8 while the department figure is 27133.98, and the gap is unmetered load, so I'll use the department number and the difference comes to 2767.699.

input.sql: SELECT sum(CASE WHEN month_start LIKE '2026-03%' THEN kwh ELSE 0 END) - sum(CASE WHEN month_start LIKE '2026-02%' THEN kwh ELSE 0 END) AS value FROM reading WHERE meter_id='dept_d'

args.sql: SELECT sum(CASE WHEN month_start LIKE '2026-03%' THEN kwh ELSE 0 END) - sum(CASE WHEN month_start LIKE '2026-02%' THEN kwh ELSE 0 END) AS value FROM reading WHERE meter_id='dept_d'

messages.content:
Assembly used about **2,767.70 kWh more in March 2026 than in February 2026**.

| Month | Assembly consumption (kWh) |
|---|---|
| February 2026 | 27,133.98 |
| March 2026 | 29,901.68 |
| **Difference (March − February)** | **2,767.70** |

These figures come from the Assembly department's own meter. Adding up its two lines would give a smaller total, because the department meter also records some usage that neither line meter captures.

Part of the increase is because March is longer. February has 28 days of readings and March has 31; March is short only the one hour lost when clocks moved forward.
